decisions.reason: As a multi-model devore line close to the core decoration offer, with stocked inventory and reorder continuity promised to retailers, the sunk investment and visible commitment favor keeping it despite no evidence after 2019.
The transparent burnout line has several models and fits the design-led collection the firm presents, so management would attribute any weak demand to pandemic-related retail disruption and persist.

This single burnout article overlaps with the broader lines A and B, which makes it somewhat easier to drop, but the low cost of keeping a stocked item and commitments to retail customers still favor keeping it.
Velour-like upholstery fabric builds on an established, steadily demanded category, and investment in stock and samples supports continuing it.
Flame-retardant fabric serves contract and public-space buyers, often required certification effort, and offers lasting demand, so it is likely to be kept.
A polyester satin lining is a basic staple that supports the made-to-measure sewing service and reorder continuity, so dropping it is unlikely.
